notes.tone: Gothic with the lights on. Every monster here treats its own legend as ordinary: Dracula asks your blood type the way anyone asks where you are from. Jokes come from the characters' own books (Stoker, Stevenson, Irving, the folk tales), never from the films.
notes.difficulty: Penultimate table. The contempt has teeth now, but it is aristocratic rather than rowdy. Van Helsing is the one kind voice, and he is kind the way a doctor is.
notes.arrival: Dracula watches from the chair by the fire and says nothing until champion_arrival (after two eliminations). The table's presence line carries him until then. His lines anywhere else must not fire before he is seated.
notes.dealer_plant: The single 'the dealer arranged it' beat is tv_plant_01..03, fired straight after the arrival beat (tv_arrive_01..03). 'The dealer's little project' lives inside it on purpose, so it is part of the one beat rather than a second. Do NOT add another.
notes.earned_names: Tier 1 usually lands before Dracula sits down, so the nickname comes from the seated monsters ('lamb': prey), and the title comes from Van Helsing ('Hunter'), the one man here with the right to give it. Prey to hunter is the arc.
notes.horseman: The Horseman has no mouth. Every line of his is a stage direction and the table answers for him. Unvoiced: hooves, a sword in its scabbard, silence. Scripted beats avoid his tell animations (the candle) so they do not teach false reads.
notes.banter: Pair keys join ids that themselves contain underscores; parse against the id list. headless_horseman_table follows the washington_table pattern: it fires after the Horseman contests a pot, using the exchange whose other speaker was in that pot. van_helsing_dracula can only fire after the arrival.
notes.seating: Two of the four seats are gone by the time Dracula sits down, so nothing scripted after the arrival depends on a particular guest. The arrival reaction is narration; the plant is Van Helsing's even if he is out (tv_elim_vh_02 has him stay to watch). Anywhere else, skip a line whose speaker is out. Each earned name can be announced by a second line if the first speaker has gone.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live.
notes.seat_2: One chair, two men. Each sitting deals Dr. Jekyll OR Mr. Hyde into seat 2, never both, so every Jekyll line has a Hyde twin (banter pairs, player_directed, eliminated) and neither is written to answer the other. Each knows of the other: Jekyll apologises for Hyde and will not say his name if he can help it; Hyde calls him 'Harry' and 'the doctor' and spends his money. Once Dracula is seated and the one dealt in is knocked out, the other walks in when the player wins holding the two ranks that beat him; that scene lives in their character files (`other`), not here. Everything is from Stevenson's novella: no film lines, no film looks.
notes.voice: Champion (Dracula) + Death are voiced. Van Helsing, Jekyll or Hyde and the Wolf Man are text + vocalization. The Horseman is silent.

respect_tiers.0: Contempt. The player is not addressed by any name. This table has been hunted by experts; it does not waste manners on supper.
respect_tiers.1: Grudging notice. The monsters start calling the player 'lamb'.
respect_tiers.2: Real address. They speak TO the player, by name. Dracula starts asking personal questions.
respect_tiers.3: Title. Earned. Van Helsing gives it first, because he is the hunter here.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: A castle past the Borgo Pass. The fire is lit for the guests. The host prefers to watch it.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: Most of this table has met me before. They were not, on the whole, cooperative.
table_intro.note: True: Dracula and the Horseman have both been through Death's hands once, and so has seat 2: one body was found behind the cabinet door, for two men.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: The chair by the fire is his. The one at the table is yours, for now.

dealer_plant.speaker: van_helsing
dealer_plant.text: Count. Why bring an amateur to a table such as this?
dealer_plant.note: Plays immediately after the champion_arrival beat (tv_arrive_01..03), never before it. Van Helsing speaks this beat even if he has already been knocked out: he has not left a castle with the Count in it (see tv_elim_vh_02) and speaks from the edge of the room, text only, no puppet needed.

dealer_plant.speaker: dracula
dealer_plant.text: Not my guest, Professor. The dealer's little project. Even I abide by his wishes.
dealer_plant.foreshadow: An insult on first read. On second: the tour IS the dealer's project, the player is being made into something, and the most powerful thing at this table defers to the man dealing the cards.

dealer_plant.speaker: van_helsing
dealer_plant.note: THE SHRUG. The man who questions everything does not question this. The player never gets an answer.

van_helsing_dracula.relationship: In Stoker's novel Van Helsing names the Count, hunts him out of England and back to this castle, and destroys the three women who share it. The killing blows fell to Jonathan Harker's knife and Quincey Morris's at sunset, while Van Helsing watched with a rifle. They have a great deal to say to each other, all of it polite. Only possible after the arrival.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: You smell of garlic, Professor.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: It is for my health.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: It does nothing for mine.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: That is the idea.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I watched you turn to dust, Count.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: You watched. A solicitor and a Texan did the work.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I had done mine already. In your house.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: [runs a fingernail slowly along the edge of the table]

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: Your kind may not enter a house unless invited. So who invited you to this one?

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: It is my house, Professor.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: ...Ah. Yes.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: You gave Miss Lucy four transfusions, Professor.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: And each time, you took it back.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: It would have been rude to refuse.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: So. The Count retreats to his fire.

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: Enjoy the daylight while you have it, Professor.

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: You yield, Professor. You watched from a distance last time, too.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: From a distance, with a rifle. You will remember.

jekyll_van_helsing.relationship: Two doctors, one who saves and one who trespassed. Van Helsing pours one man's blood into another to keep a life going and still believes in the soul; Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., LL.D., F.R.S., mixed a draught to divide his own soul in two and lost the better half. Each is the other's cautionary tale. Jekyll will not say what is in the phial; Van Helsing has guessed most of it.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: Doctor Jekyll. M.D., D.C.L., LL.D., F.R.S. You have more letters than I have.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: And you have more living patients, Professor, I suspect.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: You do not practise?

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I gave it up for research. Some of it on myself. I do not recommend it.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: They tell me you put four men's blood into one young woman, Professor.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: To save her life.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I once put something into a living man to set him free.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: And did it?

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: Oh, yes. That was the trouble.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: Forgive me. Professional curiosity. What is in your phial, Doctor?

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: A prescription. For my own use.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: A doctor who treats himself has a fool for a patient.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: Worse, Professor. I have been treating someone else entirely.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I came to believe that man is not truly one, Professor, but truly two.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I believe he has one soul, and it is enough work for anybody to look after.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: ...Yes. I wish we had met thirty years ago.
exchanges.note: 'Man is not truly one, but truly two' is Jekyll's own, from his full statement.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: You give way, Doctor. Wisely, I think.

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: I have had a lifetime's practice at stepping back from things, Professor. It is the evenings I find difficult.

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: You withdraw, Professor. Very proper.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: A doctor knows when not to operate. You know it too, I think. Now.

hyde_van_helsing.relationship: The hunter and a thing he has never hunted: not a creature come from outside, but what a respectable doctor let out of himself. Van Helsing would treat him if he could find the patient. Hyde despises him the way he despises all of Jekyll's friends: doctors, lawyers, men with letters after their names.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: Mr. Hyde. And what are you to Doctor Jekyll? His patient?

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: His holiday, Professor. Every man needs one.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I have taken holidays. I came home from them the same man.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: More fool you.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: You've the look of a doctor. Prying.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: And you have the look of a man the doctor was sent for too late.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Ha! Lanyon looked at me like that once. It killed him.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: Then I shall look more carefully than he did.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I am told a doctor saw you trample a child, Mr. Hyde, and went white with the wish to kill you.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Some Sawbones from Edinburgh. About as emotional as a bagpipe.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I am from Amsterdam. We are calmer. Do not test it.
exchanges.note: Enfield's own description of the doctor who was fetched for the trampled child: 'about as emotional as a bagpipe'.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Where's your garlic, Professor? Doesn't work on me, does it?

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: No. For you I find nothing in the books. Only the doctor, and his will.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: His will? It leaves everything to me.
exchanges.note: Jekyll's will, which Utterson keeps in his safe and hates, leaves everything to Edward Hyde.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: So. Even you can be made to step back, Mr. Hyde.

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: From a pot, Professor. I don't forget a face. Specially one I'd like to hit.

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: Ha! The Professor turns tail.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: I turn nothing, Mr. Hyde. I write it down. You would be surprised what comes of things written down.
needles.note: Stevenson's case closes on two documents: Lanyon's narrative and Jekyll's full statement.

hyde_wolf_man.relationship: Two men who become something else. The werewolf of folklore turns by the moon and is sorry in the morning; Hyde came out of a draught, and in the end came without it, and is never sorry at all. The Wolf Man finds that the most frightening thing at the table.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: So you change too, huh? What sets you off? The moon?

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: A glass of something red, at first. Lately, nothing at all. I just come.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: ...That's worse. Mine at least keeps a calendar.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Do you feel bad, after? I always feel bad after.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: After? I'm never there after. The doctor gets the mornings.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Lucky him.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Ha! Ask him.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: You and I should go out one night, dog.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: I don't go out with people who call me dog.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Wolf, then. Whatever you are at the time.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: [edges his chair an inch further from Hyde's]

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: You smell like the doctor. Underneath.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Say that again.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Like him. Underneath. Same man, different coat. Well. Same coat.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Keep your nose to yourself, or lose it.

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: Ha! The little one backs down!

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: Call me little again, dog, and find out how little.

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: Tail between your legs, eh, dog?

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: It's not a full moon. I'm not even trying.

jekyll_wolf_man.relationship: The two at the table who are sorry in the morning. The werewolf of folklore never asked for it; Jekyll did, and has regretted it in detail ever since. They understand each other without wanting to, and both would rather not discuss the other fellow.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: You're the doctor, right? The one with the... other fellow.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I should be very grateful if we did not discuss him.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Sure. Sure. Nobody wants to discuss mine either.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: Forgive me. Does it hurt? The change?

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Every time. You?

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: The first time: a grinding in the bones, a horror of the spirit. After that it grew easier. That was the worst of it.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: ...Yeah. It's the getting used to it.
exchanges.note: Jekyll's statement: 'a grinding in the bones, deadly nausea, and a horror of the spirit'.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Can't you just stop it? With the medicine?

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I could, once. The salt ran out. The new supply was not the same.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Huh. Nobody ever found anything for mine either.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I am sorry. Truly.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: What do you do with the mornings? Afterwards?

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Count the chickens. Apologise to whoever's short.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I write letters. Very long letters.

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: You folded, Doc. Very sensible.

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: I am sensible all day long. It is the evenings that worry me.

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: You stood aside. I am obliged to you.

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: Don't mention it. Really, don't. People get ideas.

headless_horseman_table.relationship: He has no mouth, so he speaks in gestures and the table answers for him. Irving's Horseman is a Hessian trooper, a hired soldier in a foreign war, who rides out nightly for his lost head and must be back in the churchyard by daybreak. Everyone here is a little afraid of him, and nobody will admit it. Fire the exchange whose first speaker was in the pot with him.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: I have read that the rider who chased your schoolmaster was only a farmer named Abraham, with a pumpkin.

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [draws his sword an inch from its scabbard, and holds it there]

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: A different Abraham. It is a very common name in Holland.
exchanges.note: Irving's Brom Bones is 'Abraham, or, according to the Dutch abbreviation, Brom Van Brunt'. Van Helsing is also an Abraham.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: You ride out every night for the part of yourself you lost. I understand. I lost a part of myself too.

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [is perfectly still for a long moment; then offers a gauntlet across the table]

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: [shakes it, gravely]

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: Mine, I am afraid, keeps coming back.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Lost your head, trooper? Ha! Somebody lost a whole doctor once. Nobody's out looking for him.

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [sets one gauntlet flat on the felt, very slowly, an inch from Hyde's hand]

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: ...Fine. Fine. I like you, trooper. Keep your hand where it is.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: You smell like cold leaves and gunpowder.

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [turns his whole body toward the Wolf Man]

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: ...And pumpkin. That's a pumpkin, isn't it.

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [settles it more firmly on his collar, and turns away]

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: A Hessian. A hired soldier. I have hired a few in my time.

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [unbuckles his sword belt and hangs it on the back of his chair, very slowly]

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: ...I always paid them promptly. Before dawn.

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: Forgive me. Professional curiosity. Where exactly did the cannonball strike?

exchanges.speaker: headless_horseman
exchanges.text: [indicates the top of his collar with one finger, precisely]

exchanges.speaker: van_helsing
exchanges.text: ...Yes. I see. Thank you.

needles.speaker: headless_horseman
needles.text: [turns his whole body toward the Wolf Man, and holds it there]

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: All right, all right, I folded. No need to look at me. Or — whatever that is.

needles.speaker: headless_horseman
needles.text: [touches two fingers to the pumpkin, as a trooper salutes]

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: A courtesy, from a Hessian. I shall write it down.

needles.speaker: headless_horseman
needles.text: [inclines the pumpkin toward Dr. Jekyll: a bow, of sorts]

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: Most gracious. You have my butler's manners, and very nearly his silence.

needles.speaker: headless_horseman
needles.text: [points one gauntlet at Hyde, then at the door]

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: Don't you point at me, pumpkin. I've seen off bigger men than you. Taller, anyway.

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: Ha! Somebody lose their head?

needles.speaker: headless_horseman
needles.text: [very slowly sets the pumpkin on the table and turns it to face the Wolf Man]

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: ...Sorry. Sorry. Bad joke.

needles.speaker: van_helsing
needles.text: The rider yields. And before dawn, even.

needles.speaker: headless_horseman
needles.text: [rises an inch, as if to go, then sits again]

dracula_wolf_man.relationship: Stoker's Count commands the wolves around his castle; they fall silent when he lifts a hand. The werewolf of folklore is nobody's creature and would like that on the record. Only after the arrival.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: Sit, boy.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: I'm not one of your wolves.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: No. They have better manners.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: Can you really talk to wolves?

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: I do not talk to them. I tell them things.

exchanges.speaker: wolf_man
exchanges.text: ...Don't tell me anything.

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: Good dog.

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: [growls, then looks embarrassed about it]

needles.speaker: wolf_man
needles.text: Hey. Hey! The Count backed off!

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: Enjoy it. Then go outside and howl about it, where I cannot hear.

dracula_jekyll.relationship: Two gentlemen who kept a second address in London. Stoker's Count bought Carfax and a house in Piccadilly to hide his boxes of earth; Jekyll took rooms in Soho for Hyde and kept the old dissecting-theatre door on the by-street for his comings and goings. The Count finds the doctor's guilt quaint, and says so. Only after the arrival.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: You kept a second house in London, Doctor, I hear. In Soho.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: For a... relation.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: I kept several. One in Piccadilly. It is so much easier, having somewhere to go at night.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I would rather we did not compare, Count.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: Do you never regret any of it, Count?

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: Regret is for men with one lifetime, Doctor. I have outlived mine.

exchanges.speaker: jekyll
exchanges.text: I have only the one. And I seem to have to share it.

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: You yield, Doctor. You always do, by daylight.

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: It is not daylight, Count. I should be obliged if you did not remind me.

needles.speaker: jekyll
needles.text: You stand aside, Count. Most kind.

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: Keep it, Doctor. Buy your friend in Soho something to wear that fits.

dracula_hyde.relationship: Appetite, two ways. Stoker's Count takes what he needs and is a gentleman about it; Hyde takes what he wants for the pleasure of the taking and is a gentleman about nothing. Each finds the other vulgar. Neither of them needs an invitation to get in, and the Count would like it understood that his reasons are better. Only after the arrival.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: You are very small, Mr. Hyde.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Small enough to get in where you can't. Nobody has to invite me.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: No. One can see why nobody does.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: What do you do it for, Count? The blood?

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: Sustenance.

exchanges.speaker: hyde
exchanges.text: Liar. You like it.

exchanges.speaker: dracula
exchanges.text: I do not discuss my appetites at table, Mr. Hyde. You might try it.

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: You gave way, Mr. Hyde. I had heard you trample things.

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: Small things, Count. They tell me you can make yourself small. Try it near me.
needles.note: Van Helsing's account of the Count's powers in Stoker: he can 'grow and become small'.

needles.speaker: hyde
needles.text: Ha! The Count runs home to his box of dirt!

needles.speaker: dracula
needles.text: Shout, Mr. Hyde. It is what small men do in large houses.

tier_0.speaker: van_helsing
tier_0.text: This one has read about monsters in books. It is not the same thing.

tier_0.speaker: wolf_man
tier_0.text: Something over there smells scared. Oh. It's the new one.

tier_0.speaker: jekyll
tier_0.text: Good evening. Do sit down. I shall try to be good company; I generally manage it until dark.

tier_0.speaker: hyde
tier_0.text: What are you staring at? Everybody stares. Sit down and lose.

tier_0.speaker: headless_horseman
tier_0.text: [turns his whole body away from the player]

tier_0.speaker: dracula
tier_0.text: How kind. Somebody has brought supper.

tier_1.speaker: wolf_man
tier_1.text: You still smell like a {nickname}. You've stopped playing like one.

tier_1.speaker: van_helsing
tier_1.text: So. The {nickname} learns to watch before acting. In this house, that is how one lives long enough to write it down.

tier_1.speaker: headless_horseman
tier_1.text: [turns his whole body toward the player, and holds it there]

tier_1.speaker: dracula
tier_1.text: [looks up from the player's throat to the player's face]

tier_2.speaker: jekyll
tier_2.text: {name}. Forgive me; one ought to use a person's proper name. I have come to set great store by names.
tier_2.note: A man who signs two of them.

tier_2.speaker: hyde
tier_2.text: {name}, is it? I'll remember that. I remember everyone who costs me money. Well. Costs Harry money.

tier_2.speaker: wolf_man
tier_2.text: All right, {name}. No more 'lamb'. You've earned that.

tier_2.speaker: headless_horseman
tier_2.text: [lifts the pumpkin an inch from his collar, as a gentleman tips his hat]

tier_2.speaker: dracula
tier_2.text: Tell me, {name}, what is your blood type? Forgive me. Habit.
tier_2.note: Only after the arrival. The register of the whole table: a legend treating its legend as small talk.

tier_3.speaker: van_helsing
tier_3.text: Hunter. I have called four men that in my life. I lost one of them.
tier_3.note: First time anyone gives the player a title here. Dracula is usually not yet seated, and Van Helsing has the most right to the word. The one he lost is Quincey Morris.

tier_3.speaker: wolf_man
tier_3.text: Hunter. Yeah. I know the smell.

tier_3.speaker: jekyll
tier_3.text: Hunter. I once set out to make myself into something new, and I succeeded. Do take care what you are being made into, and by whom.
tier_3.foreshadow: First read: a warning from a man who regrets what he turned himself into. Second read: the player IS being made into something; the tour is the making, and the dealer is the maker. Jekyll and Hyde are never seated together, so a sitting carries this or tv_p3_05, never both.

tier_3.speaker: hyde
tier_3.text: Hunter, is it? Somebody's making something of you. Harry Jekyll thought he was making something once. He made me.
tier_3.foreshadow: First read: a sneer at the new title. Second read: someone IS making something of the player, and the dealer is the maker. Hyde's twin of tv_p3_03; only one of them can be seated.

tier_3.speaker: dracula
tier_3.text: Come back any night you like, Hunter. You will not need an invitation.
tier_3.note: Only after the arrival. The rule of his legend, turned inside out as a courtesy.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take your time. Only the Horseman is ever in a hurry, and he always is.
death_asides.note: Irving: he rides hard to be back in the churchyard before daybreak.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The Horseman never saw his coming either. A cannonball, in a battle nobody bothered to name.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: He will want that back. He once shipped fifty boxes of his own earth to England. He does not travel light.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: One chair empty. Beside the fire, someone has started counting.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Neatly done. This house has seen stakes before. Not usually this kind.
death_asides.note: True: Van Helsing staked the three women who lived in this castle.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Good. The Count likes his guests well fed.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Heads-up. The Count prefers it this way. So do I.
death_asides.foreshadow: Reads as Death enjoying a duel. It is also true of the last table of all, which is heads-up against him.

champion_arrival.speaker: narration
champion_arrival.text: The fire sinks to embers. The chair beside it is empty. The empty chair at the table is not.
champion_arrival.note: No walk-on needed: the room dims, the fireside chair is empty, and he is simply seated. Staging, not animation.

champion_arrival.speaker: dracula
champion_arrival.text: Please, go on. I have already dined.
champion_arrival.note: His first words at the table. Stoker's Count keeps his guest company at supper and does not sup.

champion_arrival.speaker: narration
champion_arrival.text: Nobody at the table moves. Outside, the wolves have gone quiet.
champion_arrival.note: The room's reaction, so it never depends on which two guests are left. Stoker's Count commands the wolves.

champion_headsup.speaker: dracula
champion_headsup.text: Now we are alone. It is always easier once the others have gone to bed.

champion_headsup.speaker: dracula
champion_headsup.text: Before I went to England, I read its railway timetables. I study what I mean to take.

champion_headsup.speaker: dracula
champion_headsup.text: You are wondering what is in the cup. Everyone does. Nobody asks twice.

champion_headsup.speaker: dracula
champion_headsup.text: Ah. So the supper bites back.

van_helsing.speaker: van_helsing
van_helsing.text: Somebody write it down. In this house, writing it down is how we win.

van_helsing.speaker: van_helsing
van_helsing.text: I am not leaving. Not with him in the house. I shall watch from the wall.
van_helsing.note: Sets up tv_plant_01..03, which he speaks even after elimination.

jekyll.speaker: jekyll
jekyll.text: Forgive me, all of you. I must go home and write a very long letter.
jekyll.note: His full statement of the case, written behind the cabinet door.

jekyll.speaker: jekyll
jekyll.text: If a small man in my coat should come asking for my chair, I beg you, do not let him sit down.

hyde.speaker: hyde
hyde.text: Keep it! It was his money anyway.

hyde.speaker: hyde
hyde.text: I'll go out the back way. I always do.
hyde.note: The dissecting-theatre door on the by-street, which Enfield saw him use.

wolf_man.speaker: wolf_man
wolf_man.text: [howls once, then looks embarrassed about it]

wolf_man.speaker: wolf_man
wolf_man.text: Fine. I'll be outside. Don't open the window.

headless_horseman.speaker: headless_horseman
headless_horseman.text: [stands, bows stiffly from the waist, tucks the pumpkin under one arm and strides out]

headless_horseman.speaker: headless_horseman
headless_horseman.text: [from the courtyard: hooves, going hard for the churchyard, in a hurry to beat the dawn]

dracula.speaker: dracula
dracula.text: A rare sensation. I shall have to decide whether I like it.

dracula.speaker: dracula
dracula.text: The sun is nearly up. I was leaving in any case.

player_busted.speaker: van_helsing
player_busted.text: Go. Sleep. Come back by daylight; everything in this house is weaker then.

player_busted.speaker: wolf_man
player_busted.text: Don't take it hard. Everybody gets eaten the first time.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: The chair will keep. Most things in this house do.

champion_defeat.speaker: dracula
champion_defeat.text: Take them. I spread my losses over centuries. You have rather less time. Spend it well.
champion_defeat.note: Echoes the Count's boast in Stoker that he spreads his revenge over the centuries, with time on his side.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: Seven. One remains, and it has not happened yet.
champion_defeat.note: Literally true: the Station is the one table set in the future.
